title: Hoover's Kabob-licious named Alabama's best hole-in-the-wall Indian restaurant
excerpt: The family-run halal Indo-Pak grill earned Alabama's slot in The Takeout's 50-state ranking of America's best hole-in-the-wall Indian restaurants.
body:
• Kabob-licious in Hoover, Alabama, has been named the state's best hole-in-the-wall Indian restaurant in The Takeout's 50-state ranking.
  • The family-run halal Indo-Pak grill is celebrated for its chicken tikka boti, grilled tikka wings, kebabs and nihari.
  • A local reviewer called its grilled tikka wings, kebabs and nihari the best in the South outside Atlanta.
  • Find it at 1841 Montgomery Highway, Suite 105, Hoover (205-407-6777); it is closed on Mondays.

Alabama's best hole-in-the-wall Indian restaurant is Kabob-licious in Hoover. The family-run halal Indo-Pak grill earned the state's slot in The Takeout's ranking of the best hole-in-the-wall Indian restaurant in every state, a 50-entry list celebrating the unassuming spots serving America's most exciting Indian food.

The Birmingham-area restaurant, on Montgomery Highway in Hoover, was singled out for its grilled meats and boldly seasoned dishes — the kind of neighbourhood joint where the food, not the decor, does the talking.

Why the hole-in-the-wall matters

The Takeout's list makes a deliberate argument: some of the best Indian food in America is served in the humblest rooms. Its picks range from strip-mall counters to gas-station kitchens, united by family ownership, low prices and fiercely loyal followings. For Alabama, the editors landed on Kabob-licious, a casual grill whose reputation has been built almost entirely by word of mouth.

The entry notes the restaurant's Chicken Tikka Botti as the dish to order, and quotes a food influencer who called it an "interesting, unsuspecting hole in the wall with a unique menu & fantastic food." A local Reddit reviewer from India went further, calling its grilled tikka wings, kebabs and nihari the best in the South apart from Atlanta.

"If you're looking for an interesting, unsuspecting hole in the wall with a unique menu & fantastic food, you've found your place."

— Food influencer, quoted by The Takeout

The Hoover pick

Kabob-licious describes itself as a halal Indo-Pak grill, and the menu leans into the tandoor: chicken tikka boti, malai boti, seekh kabob, behari kabob and lamb chops sit alongside biryanis, karahis, samosas and a short list of breads including garlic and bullet naan. Reviewers consistently praise the tenderness of the grilled meats and the generosity of the spicing, with several noting the kitchen will adjust heat levels on request.

The business is family-run, helmed by chef Mehdi Sultan, and regulars describe being treated like guests in the owners' home. Aggregated reviews put it around 4.4 to 4.6 out of 5, with the grilled platters, beef samosas and mango lassi drawing the most consistent praise. It is closed on Mondays and serves lunch and dinner through the rest of the week.

Bham Now, the Birmingham-area food and culture site, has long championed the city's international restaurants, and the statewide nod puts Kabob-licious on the map for diners well beyond Hoover.

Diaspora angle

The recognition captures a quiet shift in the American South's food landscape. Halal Indo-Pak grills like Kabob-licious — often opened by immigrant families, often in unglamorous strip malls — are winning over diners far outside the diaspora. For the region's South Asian community, it is also a point of pride: proof that the food of home can compete with anything in the state.

What's next

Statewide lists like this one tend to bring new faces through the door, and Kabob-licious's no-frills dining room may find itself busier than usual in the coming weeks. For Hoover's growing international food scene, the spotlight is another sign that some of Alabama's most interesting eating is happening off the main drag.
